question.text: How is income of AIF Category III taxed, and how does this differ from Category I and II?

answer.text: Category III has pass-through status; income is taxable only for unit-holders
All three categories have pass-through status; income is taxable only for unit-holders
Category III income is exempt; Category I and II income is taxable at the fund level

Category III does NOT have pass-through status; its income is taxed at the AIF level based on its legal structure (trust, company, LLP, or other body corporate), while Category I and II enjoy Section 115UB pass-through except for business income.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook page 284, Category I and Category II AIFs have Section 115UB pass-through status except for business income. Per page 287, this pass-through is accorded only to Category I and II AIFs and not to Category III; Category III taxation follows the AIF's legal form (normal trust, company, LLP, or other body corporate), with specified-fund exceptions. The Trap: Options A and B incorrectly extend pass-through to Category III. Option C reverses the actual position. A common over-statement is that Category III income is always taxed at the maximum marginal rate at fund level; the source instead routes taxation through the AIF's legal structure. Note: Category III's actual tax outcome depends on the legal vehicle used for the AIF and any specified-fund exceptions, not on a uniform fund-level maximum-marginal-rate rule.
